meta.note: A thin day. Kit Studio, Xsolla, Vauxhall, the taste essay and the ChatGPT ad and watermark stories already ran on 5 and 6 October and are not repeated. Left out: a large Prime Day deals wave, gadget reviews, general AI model and agent news (Mistral Large 4, Reflection Beam, OpenAI agents on Wikipedia), a Medium member-only piece on recommending instead of reporting, and all of Roastbrief's agency press releases. The userresearchstrategist.com feed failed, the State of Brand sitemap returned no pages in the window, five paid Substack posts were removed before curation.

stories.title: Good names describe purpose, not appearance
stories.blurb: Vitaly Friedman collects resources for naming components, tokens and features. Two rules carry over to any project: a name should say what something does rather than how it looks, and a feature name should come from the words users themselves use when they explain it. Also worth a look: Intuit's case study on its token taxonomy and Iain Bean's Component Gallery, which lists the alternative names of more than 50 components.

stories.title: Love And Money fit a typeface into fourteen pixels for the Orchid synth
stories.blurb: The logotype bends PP Editorial Neue with hand-drawn ligatures until it could be blooming or decaying, like a note swelling and fading. The more instructive part is the device screen: 128 by 128 pixels, characters 14 to 18 pixels tall, each pixel two high and one wide so the counters stay open enough to read.

stories.title: Jaguar chose the design that scored ones and tens
stories.blurb: Three teams in Covid bubbles each built full-size clay models. Design clinics produced polarised scores, and Jaguar deliberately preferred strong 1s, 2s, 9s and 10s over safe 5s and 6s. In a blind vote by the twelve-person executive board the most radical direction won eleven votes. A rare documented case of polarisation used as the selection metric.

sources.headline: The in-depth story behind the Jaguar Type 01 design revolution

stories.title: Disney cuts its own logo in half for Hulu
stories.blurb: Courage's outdoor campaign in Canada joins the first letters of the Hulu and Disney wordmarks into "Hu Dis?" to say that Hulu shows now sit inside Disney+. It works because half the Disney wordmark is still unmistakable. Creative Bloq offers little beyond the images.

stories.title: LibreOffice turns "no AI" into a product position
stories.blurb: The Document Foundation says it will not add AI to the default install for now and calls this a deliberate design position: documents stay on the machine and nothing needs a network connection. AI remains possible through extensions that connect to local models. A clear example of positioning by leaving something out, and relevant to anyone handling confidential client files.

sources.name: TechCrunch
sources.headline: LibreOffice says no AI is now a software feature

stories.title: Three ways a well-fitting explanation can still be wrong
stories.blurb: Researcher Saeideh Bakhshi uses Clever Hans, the Mars canals and the miasma theory to name three failure modes: the evaluation setup changes the behaviour being measured, expectation shapes what counts as evidence, and an intervention can work while resting on the wrong cause. A useful check for anyone synthesising research, at a time when machines produce coherent stories on demand.
